NDT training in Pittsburgh: how it works for Pittsburgh employers and technicians

NDT training in Pittsburgh is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, taught live online or onsite at your mill, plant, shop or field base under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training hours, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams, and a vision test.

Pittsburgh's inspection work is shaped by what the region makes and what it has to keep standing. Integrated steelmaking in the Mon Valley, specialty metals along the Allegheny, the nuclear engineering and component supply chain around Cranberry, Cheswick and West Mifflin, Marcellus and Utica gas gathering and processing across Washington, Greene and Butler counties, a polymers plant in Beaver County, and an ageing inventory of bridges that was put under a national spotlight when the Fern Hollow Bridge collapsed in January 2022. Few US cities combine heavy-section steel, nuclear quality requirements and pipeline work in the same labour market.

Atlantis NDT does not run a classroom in Pittsburgh. We serve Pittsburgh employers and technicians by delivering theory live online and bringing practical training, exams and Level III documentation to your facility. This section adds depth the overview does not: the method-by-method map to western Pennsylvania work, the certification path in order, scheduling around outages and the construction season, radiation licensing for crews that cross into Ohio and West Virginia, and the questions we hear most. Request a Pittsburgh training quote; we usually reply within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Pittsburgh

Courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for each method and level, then align to the codes and customer specifications your Pittsburgh work falls under. Where a nuclear or customer quality programme adds requirements, we flag them rather than paper over them.

MethodLevelsWhat Pittsburgh employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepThick-section weld and forging inspection, mill rolls and shafts, crane runway and structural welds, pipeline and pressure-vessel welds, bridge pins and weldsLevel I: employer entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
Phased array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection for nuclear components and heavy fabrication, pipeline girth welds, corrosion mapping at gas processing plantsConventional UT Level II expected first
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThrough-wall sizing of flaws in thick welds on vessels and heavy componentsConventional UT Level II expected first
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline and plant piping welds, castings, component radiography in the nuclear supply chainSeparate state radiation safety qualification before working with sources
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, IISurface cracks on structural and bridge welds, mill equipment, ladle and crane components, forgings, compressor station skidsNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, IIStainless and nickel-alloy components, specialty metal products, nuclear piping and valve bodiesNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Visual testing (VT)I, IIWeld acceptance in fabrication, bridge and structure condition inspection, nuclear VT-1/VT-2/VT-3 style examinations under owner proceduresNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Eddy current testing (ET)I, IISteam generator and heat-exchanger tubing, surface crack detection on components, conductivity and sorting in metals productionNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II

UT training covers sound propagation, probe and wedge selection, calibration, DAC and TCG, angle-beam weld scanning and flaw evaluation, with extra time for thick sections and forgings, which dominate steel and nuclear-supply work in the region. PAUT and TOFD cover focal laws, scan plans, encoded scanning and analysis, for technicians already confident in conventional UT. RT covers exposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance. MT is the everyday method in mills and on bridges. PT matters for the specialty alloy producers. VT underpins bridge work and nuclear visual examinations. ET suits technicians aiming at outage tubing work. Level III candidates prepare for the ASNT Basic and Method exams through ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Pittsburgh, step by step

Pennsylvania does not license NDT technicians by method. Your employer certifies you, and the process runs in this order:

  1. Employer written practice. The company's document sets training and experience hours, exams, grading, vision requirements, recertification intervals and the responsible Level III. Nuclear suppliers usually write theirs to CP-189.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the required formal training for the method and level, live online, in an arranged cohort or onsite. Recommended minimums are in our training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised, documented hours in the method on real work.
  4. General exam. Written questions on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. Written questions on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V, AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 or API 1104.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on examination of specimens with known discontinuities. A Level III administers and grades all three exams.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by the employer, signed by the responsible Level III, and retained for audit.
  9. Recertification. On the interval the written practice sets. Changing employer means being recertified under the new employer's practice.

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Pittsburgh crews

  • Live online theory: instructor-led classroom hours in real time, which suits field technicians working rotations at gas sites or crews on shift at the mills. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility: theory, practical and exams at your mill, plant, shop or yard, using your equipment and specimens cut from the product you actually inspect.
  • Blended: theory online, then an in-person practical and exam block. No credible scheme permits a remote practical exam.

Pittsburgh scheduling follows three calendars. Nuclear refuelling outages at Beaver Valley and elsewhere absorb qualified technicians for weeks, so train beforehand. Mill maintenance outages are planned and short. Bridge and pipeline construction work peaks between spring and late autumn, and winter is the practical window for classroom-heavy training of field crews. Tell us your calendar and we will plan around it. Ask about onsite training for your Pittsburgh crew, or see corporate NDT training.

Where NDT technicians work in Pittsburgh

Steel and specialty metals. The Mon Valley mills at Braddock, Clairton and West Mifflin, now part of Nippon Steel after its 2025 acquisition of U.S. Steel, run continuous plant-integrity and maintenance inspection: MT and UT on crane runways, ladles, rolls and shafts, and weld inspection on repairs. Specialty alloy producers along the Allegheny River add PT and ET on stainless and nickel-alloy products, and forgers and foundries in the region inspect castings and forgings to customer specifications.

Nuclear engineering and components. Westinghouse's headquarters in Cranberry Township, Curtiss-Wright's pump and motor operations in Cheswick, the Naval Nuclear Laboratory's Bettis site in West Mifflin, and Beaver Valley Power Station in Shippingport make Pittsburgh a nuclear town. Component manufacturing and in-service inspection follow ASME Section III and Section XI, with personnel qualification to CP-189 and suppliers under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and NQA-1 quality programmes. These employers add their own performance demonstrations and procedures; an SNT-TC-1A course builds the method foundation but does not substitute for them.

Natural gas. Marcellus and Utica producers and midstream operators run gathering lines, compressor stations and processing plants across southwestern Pennsylvania, eastern Ohio and northern West Virginia. Pipeline construction welding follows API 1104, and plant piping and vessels follow ASME B31.3, B31.8 and Section VIII. RT and UT on girth welds, and UT thickness and MT at compressor stations, are the bread-and-butter work.

Petrochemicals. The Monaca polymers plant in Beaver County brings refinery-style mechanical-integrity work: thickness surveys, PAUT corrosion mapping and exchanger ET.

Bridges and infrastructure. Allegheny County has hundreds of bridges, and after the Fern Hollow collapse the scrutiny of bridge inspection, including fracture-critical members, has intensified. Steel bridge welding is governed by AWS D1.5, and inspection draws on VT, MT and UT. Rail manufacturing north of the city adds weld and component inspection.

Radiography licensing. Pennsylvania is an NRC Agreement State; radioactive-source industrial radiography is licensed by the Department of Environmental Protection's Bureau of Radiation Protection, and radiographers must meet state radiation safety training and certification rules on top of SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Ohio is also an Agreement State, regulated by the Ohio Department of Health. Crews working gas jobs in West Virginia should confirm the current jurisdiction and reciprocity rules before mobilising. Our RT courses teach the method; they do not replace radiation safety requirements.

What local employers ask for. Level II in UT and MT is the most requested combination, with PAUT increasingly expected for nuclear and pipeline work. Nuclear employers want CP-189-compliant records and clean vision tests. Some local employers also ask for AWS CWI or API 653 credentials; Atlantis does not train for those schemes. For pay context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Pittsburgh NDT companies

Many Pittsburgh inspection companies serve two very different customer types: a steel mill or gas operator that expects SNT-TC-1A records, and a nuclear supplier that audits to CP-189 and Appendix B. A written practice that does not address both will not pass the stricter audit. Atlantis reviews or writes your NDT written practice to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 as your customers require, provides outsourced Level III services for exams, procedure approval and certification, writes method procedures to your customers' codes, and audits certification files before your customers do. Book a Level III consultation for your Pittsburgh company. Background reading: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT, our 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Pittsburgh candidates can rehearse weld scanning and set-up sequences between sessions. It is practice only; it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and Level III sign-off for Atlantis cohorts delivered online and onsite.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Pittsburgh

How do I get NDT certified in Pittsburgh?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer that performs NDT, complete the training and supervised experience its written practice requires, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you.

Can I take NDT training online in Pennsylvania?

Yes for classroom hours, where your employer's written practice accepts live online delivery. The practical training and practical exam are always in person on real specimens.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the training and experience hours your employer's written practice sets and on how much documented experience you already have. See the training requirements matrix. Supervised experience usually takes longer to accumulate than the classroom portion.

Do I need a license for radiography in Pennsylvania?

Working with radioactive sources requires compliance with Pennsylvania DEP radiation safety rules, including radiographer training and certification, under a company licence. That is in addition to SNT-TC-1A certification in RT.

What does NDT training cost in Pittsburgh?

We quote on request, based on method, level, group size, delivery mode and whether exams and Level III support are included. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Pittsburgh employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard basis for employer certification in steel, fabrication, gas and infrastructure work in western Pennsylvania. Nuclear employers typically certify to CP-189, which is built on the same ASNT framework.

What is the difference between SNT-TC-1A and CP-189?

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice that each employer adapts through its written practice. CP-189 is a standard with mandatory requirements, and it is the one ASME Section XI references for nuclear in-service inspection personnel.

Which method should I learn first for Pittsburgh work?

MT and UT. MT gets you working in mills, shops and on bridges quickly, and UT is the method most in demand across steel, nuclear and gas work.

Can you train our crew at our mill or plant?

Yes. Onsite delivery is our standard model for groups across western Pennsylvania and neighbouring Ohio and West Virginia.

Is bridge inspection NDT different?

The methods are the same, but acceptance criteria follow bridge welding and owner specifications such as AWS D1.5, and bridge inspection programmes have their own inspector qualification rules set by the owner and federal requirements.

Do you offer CWI or API 653 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Pittsburgh employers also ask for those credentials, which are earned through their own schemes.

Can my company outsource its Level III?

Yes. Ask about outsourced Level III support in Pittsburgh.
